stem:
The 150 oranges in a random sample from a certain supplier were weighed and the masses, $X$ grams, were recorded. The results are summarised below.

$$n = 150 \qquad \sum x = 14\,910 \qquad \sum x^2 = 1\,525\,000$$

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Calculate a 99% confidence interval for the population mean of $X$.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: The supplier claims that the mean mass of his oranges is 100 grams. Use your answer to part **(i)** to explain whether this claim should be accepted.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: State briefly why the sample should be random.
